title: The Coming Technological Singularity
subtitle: How to Survive in the Post-Human Era
publisher: VISION-21 Symposium, NASA Lewis Research Center (NASA CP-10129)
pitch: The essay that made 'the Singularity' famous: within thirty years we will be able to create superhuman intelligence, and shortly after the human era will end.

chapters.g: Two sentences that set the agenda for thirty years of debate.
Four ways superhuman intelligence might come (AI, networks waking up, human computer links, biology) and why the change after it would be as big as the rise of human life.
Vinge doubts it can be stopped, because the competitive advantage is too great, and discusses I. J. Good's idea of a docile machine.

chapters.t: Other Paths to the Singularity: Intelligence Amplification
chapters.g: Instead of building separate AI, amplify human intelligence with computers, which might keep humans in the loop.

chapters.t: Strong Superhumanity and the Best We Can Ask for
chapters.g: What a world of superhuman minds might be like, and the most we could hope for.
Vinge's reading list, from Good and Moravec to science fiction.

ideas: Superhuman intelligence would be an event horizon we cannot see past.
It may be impossible to avoid because the advantages are too great.
Intelligence amplification is a path that keeps humans involved.

args.c: It did not arrive by 2023, though by 2026 AI is doing much of the work of building AI.

quotes.text: Within thirty years, we will have the technological means to create superhuman intelligence. Shortly after, the human era will be ended.

questions: Vinge wrote in 1993. How close was his thirty year guess?
Is intelligence amplification safer than building separate AI?

quiz.q: Where was Vinge's essay first presented?
quiz.w: The VISION-21 Symposium, sponsored by NASA Lewis Research Center, in March 1993.

o: Using computers to make humans smarter
quiz.w: Vinge saw it as another path to the Singularity.
